Hi Alice,

Thanks — summarized answers below. I kept them concise; attaching a one-page retention matrix and the relevant SLA excerpt for the contract team (see attachments). Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you need walkthroughs.

1) Data residency
- Default: customer request/response payload metadata and operational logs are stored in the primary region associated with the customer account. For accounts created from EU billing/region we default to eu-west-1; US customers default to us-west-2; APAC customers default to ap-southeast-1.
- Caching: ephemeral token/KV caches live on the serving cluster and are not written to long-term storage.
- Backups: persistent backups for infrastructure snapshots are replicated to a single DR region (paired region) within the same geographic bloc by default (e.g., us-west-2 <-> us-east-1).

2) Retention windows
- Request/response payloads: Default 30 days retention for troubleshooting and billing aggregation. Customers may opt-in to longer logging for debugging; opt-in is explicit and logged.
- Aggregated telemetry: 13 months (default) for analytics and cost/usage reporting.
- Persistent artifacts (embeddings, fine-tune snapshots): Retained until customer deletes them; deletion is an explicit API action and logged. For Shared/Hosted models we keep derived embeddings only if customer explicitly stores them.

3) Deletion & expunge process
- Workflow: Customer submits an erasure request via Console or API -> request routed to data-lifecycle service -> items marked for expunge -> asynchronous purge job removes primary objects and submits removal to backup lifecycle.
- Backups: Backup expiry is handled by our backup lifecycle policy. For standard hosted customers, expunge enqueues removal from live backups; final removal depends on backup retention cycle (up to 90 days). For enterprise customers we can accelerate backup destruction via contractual addendum and certificate of destruction.
- Time to complete: Typical complete removal from primary storage: 24–72 hours. Final removal including backup slices: up to 90 days unless contract states otherwise.
- Attestation: We can provide a deletion attestation report (signed) for enterprise customers after purge completion.

4) Escrow / disaster recovery
- We do not escrow customer plaintext prompts by default. For DR we maintain encrypted persistence snapshots for platform configuration and required metadata; snapshots are encrypted with customer-tenant keys where required and accessible only to the platform infra team under strict access controls.
- Retention: DR snapshots retained for a maximum of 90 days by default; can be adjusted under enterprise terms.

5) Contractual options
- Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support hard region locks and contract-enforced retention/expunge SLAs. For Hosted API customers we offer contractual addenda for geo-locking data, accelerated backup purge, and escrow arrangements for regulated customers (requires legal review and minimal additional fees).

Attachments included: hostedapi-retention-matrix.pdf (retention windows & default behaviours), SLA_excerpt.pdf (sample contract language for retention/escrow).

Let us know which items you want formalized in the MSA or a separate addendum and we will follow up with legal.
